title: Playing the same chorus over again
summary: Whether Preservation Hall musicians enjoy playing, and the habit of repeating set solos.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Now, do you think that at preservation there's that same kind of spirit to a certain extent? I mean, first of all, you do have an enthusiastic audience. Do the musicians, you think, enjoy playing?
Yeah, they seem to respond to...
I mean, they don't play the same song over again twice, that's for sure, but they...

On the other hand, of course, where they play things over and over, all the musicians are that way, and have been here for years, that they play everything a good deal the same way. A lot of it's sort of cut and dried, yet it doesn't sound that way, because they do put themselves into it, and a lot of enthusiasm usually, but a lot of times they'll play the same chorus, more or less, over and over again. Even the, probably original Dixieland did that on the very first records, where they recorded tunes several times. They weren't... Hardly any of them could read. I think maybe Edwards was the only one, was he? Shields, probably a little. But they would still sort of get into maybe set solo. We don't know what they did, because we didn't hear the band that much, except on records. But they probably have always done that a good deal, that they would get on... Something that they play, a certain chorus that they like a good deal, they would not necessarily try to duplicate it consciously, but they would naturally, if they like that thing and it turns out good, fits everything good, they'll play mostly the same thing again.
So, it's always been that way, I think.
